result:
The answer 7 matches a published classification that I am recalling from memory; I could not check it here.

I recall the result as: graphs with no induced subdivision of H have bounded clique-width if and only if H is an induced subgraph of the gem or of co-(P₂+P₃).

- The gem is P₄ joined to a dominating vertex. It has 5 vertices and 4 + 3 = 7 edges.
- co-(P₂+P₃) is the complement of P₂+P₃. The complete graph K₅ has 10 edges and P₂+P₃ has 1 + 2 = 3 edges, so the complement has 7 edges. Equivalently, it is 2K₁ joined to (K₂+K₁), with 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 edges.
- Neither graph is an induced subgraph of the other, so both are maximal. The set of edge counts is therefore {7}, and its sum is 7.

Solution 1 claims that 𝓜 = {P₄}. This is wrong, because the gem and co-(P₂+P₃) both have 5 vertices and satisfy the property. Solution 2 claims that 𝓜 = {C₃, P₄}. This is also wrong, since C₃ is contained in the gem and so cannot be maximal.

Solution 3 reaches 7, but its derivation is incorrect. It asserts that no graph on 5 or more vertices survives, and that the maximal graphs are P₄ and the paw, giving edge counts {3, 4}. Those edge counts happen to sum to 7, so the final number agrees with the classification only by coincidence. Among the three, it is the only one whose final answer is correct.

CHOICE: 3
